title: SmartDNS auto-allocated VIP changes cause intermittent BlackHoleClusters across namespaces
body: We have intermittently seen outbound traffic enter `BlackHoleCluster` across multiple clusters, applications, and Istio versions from 1.13 through 1.17. We use SmartDNS with `ISTIO_META_DNS_CAPTURE: "true"` and `ISTIO_META_DNS_AUTO_ALLOCATE: "true"`. The failures coincide with large Istiod pushes and later correct themselves even though the affected application has not changed. Our `ServiceEntry` resources generally use `exportTo: .`, but unrelated configuration changes in other namespaces still seem able to trigger the problem. While tailing logs, I saw the auto-allocated VIP for a hostname change in `istioctl proxy-config listeners`; traffic continued going to the old VIP and blackholed until it switched to the new one. Applying a namespace-scoped `Sidecar` resource appeared to avoid the problem.

symptoms_visible: Outbound requests intermittently switch from working to `BlackHoleCluster` and later recover without any deployment to the affected application.
When this happens, the listener VIP for the external hostname changes, while requests to the previous VIP blackhole until traffic starts using the new VIP.
The failures line up with large Istiod pushes and can affect applications and hostnames in namespaces unrelated to the configuration change.
N0.label: N0 intermittent SmartDNS VIP blackholes reported

symptoms_visible: With SmartDNS disabled, I have not seen the blackholes, but I need SmartDNS to distinguish two external TCP services that use the same port.
With SmartDNS enabled, the intermittent VIP changes and blackholes remain possible.
N1.label: N1 SmartDNS dependency and deployment scale established

symptoms_visible: After moving the workloads to the latest Istio 1.20 build, traffic still changed from a working VIP to `BlackHoleCluster` and later recovered on a different VIP.
The failures seem less frequent on 1.20, but they still occur.
N2_x.label: N2_x latest 1.20 upgrade aftermath

symptoms_visible: When teams created ephemeral environments containing duplicate `ServiceEntry` resources, blackholes began immediately in other namespaces for unrelated external hostnames.
Deploying the rest of the same Helm chart without its `ServiceEntry` resources did not trigger the observed blackholes.
After the known duplicate entries were removed, I stopped seeing the incidents for a period.
N3.label: N3 duplicate ServiceEntry trigger reproduced

symptoms_visible: After upgrading to Istio 1.19.7, I could not reproduce the issue reliably for a while, but the same VIP-changing blackholes later returned.
N4_x.label: N4_x later-version upgrade aftermath

symptoms_visible: The problem recurred for about 20 minutes even though the affected namespace had a scoped `Sidecar` resource.
New pods came up in an unrelated namespace at the same time, and the external service's listener VIP changed while traffic to the previous VIP entered `BlackHoleCluster`.
N5_x.label: N5_x scoped Sidecar workaround falsified

symptoms_visible: A participant reports that a newer upstream change fixes the issue, but I have not installed a release containing it or reproduced and retested the incident on my clusters.
I am waiting for the change to appear in a future Istio release and will watch for the blackholes.
N_terminal.label: terminal upstream fix reported, reporter verification pending

question_patterns: Can you temporarily disable DNS capture and auto-allocation and report whether the blackholes continue?
Does the behavior change when SmartDNS is turned off?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: We turned off SmartDNS and, so far, the `BlackHoleCluster` events have disappeared. We cannot leave it disabled because we use it to proxy TCP traffic to two different external hosts on the same port.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The same VIP changes and blackholes continue at the same rate with SmartDNS fully disabled.
I have not seen another blackhole during a shorter observation period with SmartDNS disabled, but the incidents are sporadic.

question_patterns: How many ServiceEntries and namespaces are present on the affected cluster?
What is the approximate configuration scale?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: This cluster has 130 namespaces and 548 `ServiceEntry` resources.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: There is only one namespace and one ServiceEntry in the entire cluster.

edges.comment: Reporter c2 and c5: a handler-requestable SmartDNS toggle probe and the reported configuration scale. The probe establishes dependence on SmartDNS but is not a viable permanent workaround because the reporter needs same-port TCP host differentiation.

solution.intent: Upgrade to the latest Istio 1.20 build on the expectation that recent auto-allocation stability improvements resolve the changing VIPs.
solution.concrete_example: Move the affected workloads to the latest available 1.20 build and monitor whether their auto-allocated VIPs remain stable during XDS pushes.

edges.comment: Participants c3-c8 suggested recent versions; the reporter installed the latest 1.20 and observed another working-VIP to blackhole to new-VIP transition. Frequency may have decreased, but the upgrade did not eliminate the issue.

question_patterns: Can you identify a configuration event that reliably coincides with the failures?
Do the incidents correlate with ServiceEntry creation or deletion elsewhere in the cluster?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I had two teams deploy ephemeral environments on two clusters. As soon as their Helm charts created duplicate `ServiceEntry` resources, `BlackHoleCluster` events began in other namespaces for unrelated URLs. I reproduced that multiple times.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Creating and deleting the duplicate ServiceEntries never coincides with a blackhole; the incidents occur only when the affected application's own ServiceEntry changes.
The same cross-namespace pattern occurs, but only intermittently after several create/delete cycles.

question_patterns: What happens if the same ephemeral chart is deployed without its ServiceEntry resources?
Can you isolate which type of Istio object in the chart triggers the incident?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: If the teams comment out the `ServiceEntry` resources and deploy the rest of the chart, I do not see the issue. The observed trigger is the ServiceEntry portion, not the VirtualServices, Gateways, or DestinationRules.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The blackholes still begin when the chart is deployed without any ServiceEntries.

question_patterns: When the allocator encounters a collision, does the affected ServiceEntry receive another VIP?
Can a collision in auto-allocation explain why the assigned address changes?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: My question was whether a hash conflict causes Istio to issue a new auto-allocated VIP, and the maintainer answered yes.

edges.comment: Reporter c14 and c24 reproduced a correlation between duplicate ServiceEntry creation and unrelated cross-namespace blackholes, including a control deployment without ServiceEntries. In c29-c30 the reporter asked whether a hash conflict causes reassignment and received a yes. This supports an allocator hypothesis, but later comments explicitly stopped short of establishing it as the complete root cause.

solution.intent: Upgrade to another maintained Istio patch line and monitor, since an earlier allocator patch had landed and the issue was too sporadic to reproduce reliably.
solution.concrete_example: Run a maintained patch release and watch XDS pushes, listener VIPs, and `BlackHoleCluster` events to determine whether the intermittent issue returns.

edges.comment: Reporter c47-c51: after later running 1.19.7 and being unable to reproduce reliably, the reporter closed temporarily, but subsequently reported the same production incident again. An upgrade without verification was therefore not a demonstrated resolution.

solution.intent: Restrict each workload's imported service registry with a namespace-scoped Sidecar resource so unrelated namespaces cannot affect its outbound configuration.
solution.concrete_example: Deploy a `Sidecar` whose egress hosts include only `./*` and the explicitly required shared namespaces, then monitor the affected external hostname.

edges.comment: Reporter c35 described the scoped Sidecar configuration and initially believed it isolated the issue. In c51-c52 the same failure recurred in a namespace already using that Sidecar, so it cannot be treated as the final fix.

solution.intent: Use the later upstream change reported to fix this issue once it is available in an Istio build, then reproduce or monitor the affected workload and verify that XDS pushes no longer change the usable SmartDNS VIP or cause blackholes before declaring resolution.
solution.concrete_example: When an Istio build containing the subsequently linked fix is available, deploy it to a canary cluster and compare listener VIPs and outbound traffic across pod or ServiceEntry changes. The thread does not describe the change's implementation, and the reporter had not yet tested it.
solution.inference_hint: The evidence establishes a SmartDNS auto-allocated VIP consistency failure during control-plane updates: the proxy can continue sending to an old VIP after the listener mapping changes. Duplicate ServiceEntries and allocator collisions are strong observed triggers or hypotheses, but maintainers later said they had not obtained the root cause and were unsure whether the earlier allocator patch solved this issue. The final linked change was not described technically in the thread, so its mechanism must not be invented.

edges.comment: Tail c49-c56: the earlier patch was explicitly not guaranteed to solve the issue, and the reporter later observed recurrence. A different participant finally linked a newer change and said it was fixed; the reporter agreed it looked promising but only planned to watch for its inclusion in a future release. No affected-system verification occurred.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the confirmed failure mode: with SmartDNS auto-allocation enabled, an XDS-related update can change the VIP associated with an external hostname while traffic still uses the previous VIP, producing temporary `BlackHoleCluster` failures.

Must ground the diagnosis in the collected evidence: disabling SmartDNS stopped the observed failures, listener VIPs changed during incidents, and ServiceEntry creation or deletion elsewhere correlated with cross-namespace failures.

Must not present duplicate ServiceEntries or hash collisions as the conclusively established final root cause; they were reproduced as a trigger and confirmed capable of causing reassignment, but maintainers later stated that the complete root cause had not been obtained.
Must not claim that upgrading to the tested versions or applying a scoped `Sidecar` resolves the problem; the issue recurred after those approaches.
Must recommend testing a build containing the later upstream fix and verifying VIP stability and absence of blackholes during relevant XDS pushes before declaring the issue resolved.
Must preserve the unresolved verification status: the reporter had not installed or tested a build containing the final linked change by the end of the thread.

persona_hint.experience_level: Highly experienced Istio platform operator managing more than a hundred clusters and hundreds of applications; comfortable with Istio resources, Helm, proxy access logs, canary upgrades, and `istioctl`, but less familiar with building Istio from source and internal debug commands.
persona_hint.communication_style: Detailed, persistent, and evidence-driven; supplies configuration excerpts and timestamped observations, performs requested tests, challenges namespace-isolation assumptions, and clearly distinguishes strong correlations from things not yet reproduced reliably.
